Nilu Bag vs Unknown on 24 March, 2026
24.03.2026
Item no. 70.
Court No.8.
 Ab
(Rejected)
 Cra (Db) 490 of 2025
 With
 Cran 2 of 2026

In the matter of : Nilu Bag
 ......Appellant/
 Applicant.

Mr. Joydeep Biswas,
 Mr. Amanul Islam,
 Mr. Sourav Mukherjee
 Mr. Koushik Ghosh ......for the Appellant/Applicant.

Ms. Amita Gour,
 Ms. Afreen Begum ......for the State.
Dictated by Apurba Sinha Ray, J.
In re : CRAN 2 of 2026 1.
Learned Counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner has been falsely implicated in this case since he is the unfortunate husband of the victim.
He is in custody for about eight years two months.
There are sufficient loopholes in the judgment under appeal since the learned Trial Judge did not consider the available evidence on record in its proper perspective.
The death of his wife was accidental in nature but the learned Trial Judge convicted the petitioner under Sections 498A/302 of the Indian Penal Code and sentenced him to suffer life imprisonment.
There is no chance of an early hearing of the present appeal.
The petitioner may be enlarged on bail on any condition since he is in custody for a long period of time.
2. Learned Advocate has also submitted that the petitioner has no criminal antecedents.
The petitioner was the person who took his wife to the hospital and shouted at that relevant point of time to make the neighbours aware that his wife had committed suicide.
3. Learned Counsel for the State opposes the prayer for bail.
According to her, the accompanying sister was drugged by the present petitioner with a view to commit the offence in the unconscious state of the P.W.3, sister of the victim.
The post mortem report shows that the victim was murdered with the help of a "nora".
There is sufficient incriminating material against the petitioner and as such, she opposes the prayer.
4. We have considered the material on record.
It appears that the deposition of P.W.3 is sufficient to show how the incident occurred in the room of the present petitioner.

We do not find any Nilu Bag vs Unknown on 24 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183213794/
1 explanation under Section 106 of the Indian Evidence Act from the side of the petitioner as to how the unnatural death of his wife took place.
The post mortem report shows that the deceased sustained head injury which is ante mortem in nature.

The defence that the victim might have died due to fall on a "nora" is completely discarded in the cross examination of the P.W.12, the doctor,
who conducted the post mortem examination upon the deceased.
It is true that the petitioner is in custody for a considerable period of time.
However, it appears that the judgment of conviction was passed in the year 2022 and the appeal was filed in the year 2025.

5. It also appears from the evidence on record that on the date of the alleged incident, there was a serious altercation between the victim and her in-laws including the present petitioner over dowry demand.
6. In view of the aforesaid, we are not inclined to allow this application.
7. CRAN 2 of 2026 is dismissed.

8. We clarify that the observations made by us in this order are only for the purpose of disposing of the application for suspension of sentence and the same shall have no relevance at the final hearing of the appeal.
In re : CRA (DB) 490 of 2025 9.
From a departmental note dated March 9, 2026, we find that the department called for the Trial Court Records through memo dated March 9, 2025.
10. List this matter under the heading "To Be Mentioned" on 31.03.2026 when the department shall file fresh report as regards the status of preparation of the paper book.

(Apurba Sinha Ray, J.) (Arijit Banerjee, J.)
